source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Directions in Language Models

record.file_problem: The full post text is present. It is a linkpost summarizing a linked paper, not the linked paper itself.
record.tranche_reason: It reports applying sparse autoencoders to activations in real language models and outcomes for learned features, extending the toy-model superposition idea to LLMs.
record.gate_note: The post reports textual summaries of results, but the figures themselves are not included with their underlying values. The toy-model discussion is background, not a test of toy-model geometry. Results in the comments that describe other research are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The authors train sparse autoencoders on real LLM activations (Pythia-70M/410M, plus preliminary GPT2-small results). They report whether sparse, interpretable directions can be recovered and how complete the reconstruction is. These are their own results bearing on V4 and on the completeness part of V5. The toy-model material is background only.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct, with two additions. First, the caveat is that even zero reconstruction loss would not prove each feature monosemantic. Second, the authors raise the possibility that some features are not linearly represented, which would mean superposition explains only a subset of features.
record.recipe_differences: This post summarizes sparse autoencoders trained on real LLM activations, rather than testing the toy-network method and geometry of the original superposition study. It is a linkpost overview of the linked paper.
record.method_sensitivity: Automatic interpretation improves over baselines in all but the final Pythia-70M layers; the post says feature-edit fine-grainedness increases with dictionary sparsity.
record.problems: The post provides no numerical values for most summarized comparisons and does not include the figures' underlying data. The GPT2 (small) reconstruction result is described as preliminary and non-released. The model used for several examples and for the IOI result is not stated in the post.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result bearing on the tested versions was left out.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, no geometry, no sparsity transition.
All of it: there is no test of whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity.
Stability across runs and canonicality of SAE features are not tested; only completeness is addressed.
All of it: there is no comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.
How broadly features are spread across neurons is not quantified.

missing.what: The authors report finding many context features (medical, biology, Stack Exchange, German) as an existence proof that the method recovers more than token-level features. No row records this.
missing.locator: Dictionary Features are Highly Monosemantic & Causal

missing.what: The abstract mentions Pythia-410M and MLP-layer SAEs, but the post gives no results for them. Those results are in the linked paper only.

record.verdict_notes: This is a linkpost summary; most results are given as text without numbers. The GPT2-small completeness result is preliminary and separate from the paper. The IOI and feature-example rows do not name the model. Comment-thread content is not this study's results.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overlapping nearly orthogonal feature directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The post describes the capacity account as a hypothesis but does not test whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity are not tested.
The post does not establish that all LLM features are recovered or quantify how broadly features are distributed across neurons.
Stability and canonicality of SAE features are not tested. The post discusses incomplete reconstruction and explicitly says the feature set is not complete.
There is no comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: GPT2 (small)
rows.operation_detail: Compared model perplexity after sparse-autoencoder reconstruction with the base model while assessing reconstruction completeness.

conditions.value: approximately 60 features per datapoint, approximately 10% of the residual stream dimension

rows.locator: Bonus Section: Did We Find All the Features?

relationships.condition: Pythia-70M residual stream, non-final layers; IOI feature patching; showcased features
relationships.reason: SAE features beat all baselines on autointerpretation (R1), give finer IOI edits than PCA (R3, R5), and the example feature is concentrated on apostrophes where the residual basis is polysemantic (R6).
relationships.display_finding: SAE features beat all baselines on autointerpretation and gave finer IOI edits than PCA. The example feature focused on apostrophes, where the residual basis was polysemantic.
